source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen, Texas campus is the second-largest published data center power load in Texas, at 77 MW across three buildings.

The 77 MW is IT load, not grid draw, and at 40 kW per rack it implies roughly 1,900 racks. That is a real amount of compute, but it is one campus in a state with 133 mapped data center sites, and Texas publishes capacity for fewer than one in seven of them. The published Texas total is 475 MW, so this single campus is about a sixth of all disclosed state capacity. Power capacity is the number that matters here because it is the input that cannot be substituted, and 77 MW is the figure a reader should carry away.

The certifications are the more revealing detail. HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes describe a facility built for regulated enterprise tenants, not for AI training, which carries no standard compliance requirement. Compliance-oriented space and AI compute are not the same product, and the specifications do not say whether CyrusOne intends to convert or expand. The data also does not include an announced expansion, which the suitability score lists as missing, so nothing here supports a claim about future capacity at this site.

What the data cannot answer is whether this campus will host AI workloads at all. It gives nameplate capacity, floor area, and certifications, and nothing about utilization, interconnection status, or contracted tenants. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro has established power and fiber, but the data does not place it among the largest published AI cluster regions.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
